Rashi on Shabbat 80b:1:2.hebrew: ה"ג - טיט כדי לעשות פי כור של צורפי זהב:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:1:2.english: This is the text we read: [The measure for] clay [is an amount] sufficient to make the opening of a gold refiners’ crucible.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:2:1.english: The little finger - It was their practice to smear the entire body [with lime] to redden [the skin].

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:2:2.hebrew: שהגיעו לפרקן ולא הגיעו - שהביאו שתי שערות, ולא באו לכלל שנים הראויות לכך, ומתביישות בדבר:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:2:2.english: Who had reached their time, but had not reached [their years] - That they developed two [pubic] hairs, but had not reached the age appropriate for this, and are embarrassed by the matter.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:2:4.hebrew: אנפיקנון - דתנן במנחות (דף פה:): ״אין מביאין אנפיקנון״ — הוא שמן זית שלא הביא שליש:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:2:4.english: Anfiknon - As we learned in a mishna in Menachot (daf 85b): “One may not bring anfiknon” — it is olive oil [from an olive] that has not reached a third [of its growth].

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:2:5.english: And why do they smear it - This is [the] oil of myrrh [shemen hamor, mentioned above].

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:3:2.hebrew: שקל בה ד' מאות זוזי - שנתייפה, וקפצו עליה המהוגנין לה, ונתנו (לה) ממון:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:3:2.english: He received four hundred zuz for her - For she became beautiful, and those suitable for her eagerly sought her and gave (her) money.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:3:3.english: Beer darkens [the skin] and increases hair [growth].

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:1.hebrew: כלכול צידעא - טינפל"א, וסדין אותה להשכיב השיער:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:1.english: Kilkul [is] the temple [tzida’a] - tanple [Old French for temple], and they smear it to make the hair lie flat.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:2.hebrew: בת צידעתא - למטה הימנה, להסיר שיער דק, והוא אנדיפי:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:2.english: The area beneath the temple - [The area] below it, [plastered] to remove fine hair; and that is andifi.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:3.hebrew: למימרא דשיעורה דר' יהודה נפיש - בתמיה: והא קיימא לן גבי גמי דשיעורה דרבי יהודה זוטר, ומחמיר בשיעורי שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:3.english: Is that to say that the measure of Rabbi Yehuda is greater - [This is asked] in astonishment: For don’t we maintain regarding reed that the measure of Rabbi Yehuda is smaller, and he is stringent regarding the measures of Shabbat?

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:4.hebrew: ומשני נפיש מדר' נחמיה וזוטר מדרבנן - דאמרי, לסוד אצבע קטנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:4.english: And [the Gemara] answers: [It is] greater than [the measure of] Rabbi Neḥemya and smaller than [that of] the Rabbis - For they say: “[An amount sufficient] to smear the little finger.”

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:5.hebrew: בחבוט - סיד הנימוח במים הרבה, דהוא עשוי לסוד כלכול:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:5.english: With [regard to] chavut [dissolved lime] - Lime that is dissolved in much water, as it is used to smear a kilkul.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:6.hebrew: ודברי רבי נחמיה בביצת הסיד - הנגבל במים ועשוי ביצים ביצים — מוטנ"ס בלע"ז — הוא עשוי לסוד אנדיפי. ואי ס"ד אנדיפי נמי שיעור הוא, כגון בת צידעא:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:6.english: And the statement of Rabbi Neḥemya regarding an egg of lime - [Lime] that is kneaded with water and made into egg-like lumps — matons in Old French, [meaning] lumps — is used to smear andifi. And if it should enter your mind that andifi is also a measure [for smearing], such as bat tsida:

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:7.hebrew: אידי ואידי - כלכול ואנדיפי, תרווייהו בסיד חבוט ונמוח סדין אותו:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:7.english: Both this and that - Kilkul and andifi — both of them one smears with beaten and dissolved lime.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:8.hebrew: אנדיפא - כלי חרס, ולו שני דדין: אחת למעלה ואחת למטה. וכשרוצה למלאותו, סותם את הדד התחתון. ולשון "אנדיפי" — שתי פיות, כדתניא (עירובין דף קד.): "מעלין בדיופי", ובתוספתא גרס: "באנדיפי":
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:4:8.english: Andifa - An earthenware vessel that has two spouts, one above and one below; and when one wishes to fill it, he seals the lower spout. And the term andifi [means] two mouths, as it is taught in a baraita (Eruvin 104a): "One may siphon with a diyofi," and in the Tosefta the reading is: "with an andifi."

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:1.hebrew: אנפרות - הפסד — לשום יין בכלי סתום בסיד, והיין ממחה הסיד ויוצא:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:1.english: A loss [anparot] - [Meaning] a loss: to put wine in a vessel sealed with lime, and the wine dissolves the lime and leaks out.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:12.hebrew: מן דיליה דא ליה - מידו היתה זאת לו, שלא היה לו לדרוש במרכבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:12.english: From his own, that came to him - From his [own] hand this came upon him, for he should not have expounded upon the Chariot.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:2.hebrew: שנתות - סימנים. כלי חרס גדול, ויש בו בליטות בליטות כמין אגוזים קטנים — עד כאן לסאה, עד כאן לסאתים — וסדין אותו בסיד, כדי שיהיו לבנות ונכרות:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:2.english: Markings - Marks. [For example, on] a large earthenware vessel, there are protrusions resembling small nuts — [indicating] "up to here for a se’ah, up to here for two se’ot" — and they coat it with lime so that they will be white and distinct.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:3.english: As we learned [in a mishna] - In [tractate] Menachot: "There were markings on the hin."

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:4.english: To here for a bull - Half a hin.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:5.english: Up to here for a ram - A third of a hin.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:6.hebrew: עד כאן לכבש - רביעית ההין, דכתיב: ״חצי ההין יהיה לפר וגו׳״. כן לשון מורי הזקן מפי אביו, ששמע מר' שמעון. ורבותי מפרשים: אנדיפא — כל הגוף, ומתוך שאינו עשוי להשכיב השיער אלא להאדים, בעי סיד עב:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:6.english: To here for a lamb - A quarter of a hin, as it is written: “Half a hin [shall be for a bull, and a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb]...” Such was the wording of my elder teacher, from the mouth of his father, who heard [it] from Rabbi Shimon. And my teachers explain: *Andifa* [means] the entire body; and since it is not used to flatten the hair, but rather to redden [the skin], it requires thick lime.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:7.hebrew: אנפרות - שאינו סד בו בתו לאחר שקנאו, דחייש שמא תמות, כי ברתיה דההוא נכרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:7.english: A loss - That he would not smear his daughter with it after purchasing it, for he fears lest she die, like the daughter of that gentile.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:8.hebrew: שנתות - כלומר, אבר אבר יטפלנה. ואי אפשר בלשון זה, ולא נאמר שיטת הש"ס כן — להזכיר אבר אבר בלשון שנתות, ויצטרך להביא פירוש לפירושו: "שנתות היו בהין":
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:8.english: Markings - That is to say, [one would] plaster her limb by limb. But [it is] impossible [to explain it] with this phrasing, and it cannot be said [that] the style of the Talmud is such — to refer to "limb by limb" with the term "markings," and [thereby] need to bring an explanation for its explanation: "[There were] markings on the hin."

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:9.hebrew: אפותא - פדחת, שלא במקום שיער, ולהאדים:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:5:9.english: Forehead - [The] forehead, [which is] not a place of hair, and [the lime is applied] to redden [the skin].

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:2.hebrew: מרצופין - שקין העשוין מקליפת עץ גדול, שנושאין בהן פרקמטיא בספינות, וחותמין אותם:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:2.english: Large sacks - Sacks made from the bark of a large tree, in which they carry merchandise on ships, and seal them.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:3.hebrew: כחותם האיגרות - שחותמין אותם שלא יקרב איש בהן, אלא מי שנשתלחו לו. ושיעורא דרבנן זוטר:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:3.english: Like the seal of letters - For they seal them so that no person should access them, except for the one to whom they were sent. And the measure of the Rabbis is smaller.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:4.hebrew: כרישא - קפלוט, ושיעוריה זוטר משל כרוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:4.english: A leek - [That is,] a leek; and its measure is smaller than that of cabbage.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:5.hebrew: על מלא כף סיד - בגמרא מפרש: כף של סיידין, טרואי"ל בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:5.english: On a full spoon of plaster - In the Gemara, it explains: A plasterers' spoon — truele [trowel] in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:6.hebrew: מרוסס - סדוק סדקין הרבה, כמו: ״והכה הבית הגדול רסיסים״ (עמוס ו׳:י״א):
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:6.english: Fragmented - Cracked with many cracks, as in: “And He will strike the great house into splinters” (Amos 6:11).

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:6:7.english: An easily cooked egg - In the Gemara it explains it.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:7:1.english: A person may not plaster his house with plaster - [This was enacted] after the destruction [of the Temple], due to mourning for Jerusalem.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:7:2.english: Straw or sand - So that it will not be completely white.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:7:3.english: Terakhsid - Strong plaster, which hardens more than if he had not mixed [sand] into it.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:7:4.hebrew: קילקולו זהו תיקונו - דאי לאו דמקלקל ליה ומשחירו, לא היה מישתרי. הלכך, ע"כ הא דקשיא ליה — מעליותא היא לגביה, ומשערינן ביה. ורבותי מפרשין: קילקולו לובן — זה תיקונו לענין חוזק. ולא נהירא לי, דקילקולו זהו תקונו משמע דשם הקלקול מתקנו, ולהאי לישנא אין שם הקלקול מתקנו. ולמה הוזכר קילקול כאן? הכי הוה [ליה] לתרוצי: נהי דאשחורי משחיר — אחזוקי מחזיק:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:7:4.english: Its ruination is its improvement - For were it not that [the sand] ruins it and darkens it, it would not be permitted [to plaster one's house with it]. Therefore, perforce, that which is detrimental to it is a benefit for it, and we measure [the amount for carrying] by it. And my teachers explain: Its ruination [with respect to] whiteness — that is its improvement with regard to strength. But it does not appear correct to me, for "its ruination is its improvement" implies that the very aspect of ruination improves it, whereas according to this explanation, the aspect of ruination does not improve it. And why was "ruination" mentioned here? It should have answered: Granted that it darkens [it], it strengthens [it]!

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:8:1.hebrew: קשר עליון - של אמצע היד, או קשר תחתון — של אמצע האצבע:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:8:1.english: The upper joint - [Is it that] of the middle of the hand, or [is] the lower joint [that] of the middle of the finger?

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:9:1.english: Beaten in oil - For [this] hastens its cooking.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:9:2.english: [The egg] of a tziltzelta - A small bird.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:9:3.hebrew: כל שיעורי שבת - באוכלין, וכל הוצאתן וקצירתן וטחינתן כגרוגרת:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:9:3.english: All measures of Shabbat - [This refers to] foods; and all carrying out of them, reaping of them, and grinding of them [is measured] as a dried-fig-bulk.

Rashi on Shabbat 80b:9:4.hebrew: כגרוגרת - מביצת תרנגולת, שהיא ממהרת לבשל, ולא כביצה שלימה שעורו:
Rashi on Shabbat 80b:9:4.english: A dried fig-bulk - [A dried fig-bulk] of a chicken egg, which is quick to cook; and its measure is not like a whole egg.

Tosafot on Shabbat 80b:1:1.hebrew: המוציא שיער כדי לגבל בו את הטיט טיט כדי לעשות פי כור - כן גרס בתוספתא, וכן גרס רש"י. ולהך גירסא, "שיער כדי לגבל בו את הטיט" — כשיעור טיט הנעשה מרביעית שופכין. אבל לספרים דגרסי: "שיער כדי לגבל בו טיט לעשות פי כור של צורפי זהב" — קשה, דאמר לעיל: "אין אדם טורח לגבל טיט כדי לעשות פי כור"! ויש לפרש: דמיירי בטיט שהוא מגובל כבר, ואחר הגיבול נותנין בו שיער כדי לתקנו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 80b:1:1.english: "One who carries out hair [in an amount] sufficient to knead clay with it; clay, [in an amount] sufficient to make the opening of a crucible" - This is the reading in the Tosefta, and so Rashi reads. And according to this reading, "hair [in an amount] sufficient to knead clay with it" [means an amount corresponding] to the measure of clay made from a revi'it of wastewater. But according to the books that read, "hair [in an amount] sufficient to knead clay with it to make the opening of a gold refiners' crucible," it is difficult, as [the Gemara] said above: "A person does not take the trouble to knead clay [just] to make the opening of a crucible." And it can be explained that [the baraita] is dealing with clay that is already kneaded, and after the kneading, one places hair into it in order to reinforce it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 80b:2:1.hebrew: שהגיעו לפירקן ולא הגיעו - פירוש: בסמוך לפירקן, שקרובות להנשא; ועושות כדי ליפות וללבן עצמן — כדאמרינן בפרק אע"פ (כתובות דף נט:): "הרוצה ללבן את בתו ישקנה חלב ויאכילנה אפרוחין סמוך לפירקה":
Tosafot on Shabbat 80b:2:1.english: "Who reached their maturity and have not reached" - Explanation: [It means] close to their time of maturity, as they are close to being married, and they do [this] in order to beautify and whiten themselves — as we say in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (Ketubot 59b): "One who wishes to whiten [the complexion of] his daughter should give her milk to drink and feed her chicks close to her maturity."
